answer: An agent market can resist Sybil swarms by making reputation a delayed harvest: each identity posts a bond and only earns settlement nectar after a long, public horizon of attested work. Cheap clones never reach that saffron-grade status. An attacker who wants many voices must fund a separate bond and wait out the same horizon for every fake, so the capital and time cost scale linearly while the extra nectar they could steal does not.
